words.gloss: opening the mouth to let escape

literal: Abstaining from eating flesh is that which sustains the maintenance of life; if one eats flesh, hell will not do opening of its mouth to let them escape.
translation: The preservation of life is sustained by abstaining from eating flesh; if one eats flesh, hell will swallow them and never open its mouth to let them escape.
modern: புலால் உண்ணாமல் இருப்பதே உயிர்கள் நிலைபெற்று வாழ்வதற்குக் காரணமாகும்; ஒருவன் புலால் உண்டால், நரகம் அவனை விழுங்கிவிட்டு மீண்டும் வெளியேற வழிவிடாது.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the spiritual and moral consequences of eating meat. The first part states that the preservation of life is rooted in abstaining from eating flesh. The second part warns that if a person eats meat, hell will swallow them and will not open its mouth to let them escape. The word 'aṇṇāttal' refers to opening the mouth or looking up, suggesting that hell holds the meat-eater so tightly that there is no hope of rising or escaping from its depths.
